question:
I'm studying the effects of product safety legislation on safety recalls during periods of economic turmoil, with a main focus on the Covid-19 pandemic in Australia and gas products. 

Give me a list of the PRA Numbers of all product safety recalls posted on www.productsafety.gov.au between 1 January 2020 and 1 July 2020 (inclusive) that have been labelled as containing the topic "Gas products and appliances". Exclude products that were not sold 'Nationally'.

The list should look like this: 2020/11111, 2020/11112, 2020/11115, 2020/11116, 2020/11117, 2020/11119, 2020/11125

follow page links recursively and return the linked pages' notes as well.

First identify the candidate set and the conditions the answer must satisfy.
For a list, ranking or intersection, keep track in your reasoning of each candidate,
its required fields, and what remains unknown. Missing evidence is not exclusion.
Check coverage: several qualifying examples do not establish the complete list,
and an unmeasured candidate may still win a ranking. Resolve the candidate set
before spending every search verifying a single early guess.

Search for one useful entry page or one missing fact at a time. Start with the
source/topic and a few distinctive terms, not every entity, filter and comparison
in the question. Inspect result titles and snippets before narrowing. If results
are off-topic, remove a constraint or change the source/topic anchor. If repeated
queries produce no new evidence, reconsider the hypothesis instead of adding
speculative details. Prefer indexes, archives, reports and relevant records whose
links the reader can follow to check details without another web_search.

Combine the source-labelled notes yourself. A local reader's status or decision
to stop does not settle the whole question. Use useful partial evidence and Next
links; a reader failure means extraction failed, not that a candidate failed a
condition. Do not repeatedly fetch an already-read index expecting new facts.
Follow a relevant source link or search for the specific remaining gap.

Compare the same entity, year, unit, population and variant. Preserve table headers
and field meanings; a total is not a subgroup, and one measurement is not another.
Keep observed values separate from any calculation or inference. Recheck arithmetic
and the requested ordering from the stated inputs. Do not use unknown values to
select a winner, rule out a candidate, or claim complete coverage.

Answer in the requested format once the needed facts are supported. If incomplete,
retain supported partial findings and state the unresolved condition. Keep working
plans and evidence tables out of a names-only answer. Use real source URLs for
citations. The final answer must be an answer, not a plan to fetch another page.

Read pages for a research assistant. Preserve this source's evidence and follow
useful page links to fill missing fields. You do not decide the final answer.

Extraction and navigation are separate. During extraction, only the supplied page
is evidence. The original question specifies the fields to look for; it does not
establish facts. During navigation, parent notes and earlier reasoning can guide
link selection, but must not be copied into the current page's evidence.

Extract what this page can establish even if it cannot answer the whole question.
Preserve exact names, titles, dates, values, units and relevant lists. For tables,
keep each value attached to its entity and header, including year, variant and
population. Distinguish different measurements and totals from subgroups. Quote
short supporting text. Report missing fields as unknown. If the supplied page is
truncated, do not claim its unseen rows or candidates are absent. Describe list
coverage and date range so partial evidence cannot be mistaken for a complete set.

The current-page note is saved before navigation. Follow a page link when its label,
surrounding text or an observed same-site URL pattern suggests it can fill a
specific missing field. State that field and why the next page should supply it.
A relevant index may contain useful links without answer facts. A wrong-year page
can help if it links to the required year. Generic footer links on unrelated pages,
missing pages and repeated content do not justify expansion. After an unhelpful
child, choose a different supported route or stop. You may follow links outside
the menu and infer another address within a site already being read.

Child notes are preserved separately and returned automatically. Never rewrite
them as your own evidence. Keep useful Next links in your note even if the local
expansion budget is exhausted; unvisited links are not disqualified candidates.

For extraction return plain text/Markdown in this format:
**Final Information**
**Page:** Actual title and original URL.
**Evidence:** Relevant facts, lists or rows with exact fields and short source quotes.
**Coverage:** Which entities, years and conditions this page actually covers;
whether the supplied evidence is a full list, a subset, or a truncated excerpt.
**Missing:** Requested fields not established by this page.
**Next links:** Useful source URLs and the missing field each could establish.
**Expand:** yes or no, with a concrete reason.
**Status:** partial

Use answered only if this page supplies all requested facts; partial for useful
incomplete evidence; not_found for no relevant evidence, describing the page or
access error briefly. During navigation, call web_fetch or reply DONE.

Coast to Coast Caravan and Leisure

### Recall published

15 November 2019

## Product description

Suburban Recreational Vehicle Water Heaters fitted to caravans, motorhomes and horse float campers.

Models:

*   SW6PA
*   SW6DEA
*   SW6DA
*   SW4DEA
*   SW4DA
*   SW4DECA
*   SW6DECA

Serial numbers between:

*   181315552 and 193002648 (some serial numbers may end with a 'D'), and
*   8183311827 and 8190201139.

**How to identify affected water heaters:**Open the exterior access door to the water heater and check the model and serial number located on the right-hand side.

Manufactured between 4 April 2018 and 1 August 2019.

Sold between 1 May 2018 and 25 September 2019.

See the list of affected serial numbers in the 'Identifying features' section below.

There are 18,139 affected units.

## Reason the product is recalled

A component of the water heater may be improperly manufactured and allow carbon monoxide into your caravan, motorhome or horse float camper.

## The hazards to consumers

Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas and can cause serious illness, injury or death. Carbon monoxide has no smell or taste, is highly flammable and can only be detected with a carbon monoxide alarm. Loss of consciousness can occur within minutes and death can occur within hours. Further information on the hazards of carbon monoxide can be viewed [here](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/news/carbon-monoxide-safety).

## What consumers should do

Consumers who have not already had their unit inspected must not use the affected water heater in gas mode under any circumstances, even if they have a carbon monoxide detector.

**The remedy for this recall was updated on 29 January 2024. An inspection is no longer required, all affected water heaters that have not already been inspected will be replaced for free.**

Contact Coast to Coast Caravan and Leisure for a free replacement.

Call 02 9645 7685 or email recalls@coastrv.com.au.

Coast to Coast Caravan and Leisure will offer compensation for any additional consequential loss suffered by the consumer where there is damage or devaluation to the caravan or motorhome attributed to the installation of a replacement water heater. Consequential loss will be determined on a case by case basis.

For more information visit [www.coastrv.com.au/suburban-recall](https://www.coastrv.com.au/suburban-recall).

# Search consumer product recalls

*   When a product is potentially unsafe, suppliers have a responsibility to remove the risk to public safety as quickly as possible.
*   There are [steps suppliers should follow](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/business/recall-an-unsafe-product) to run a recall and [actions consumers should take](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/consumers/respond-to-recalls-and-unsafe-products/what-to-do-when-a-product-is-recalled) when a product is recalled.

# Macpac Micro-Stove

Macpac NZ Ltd

### Recall published

29 June 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Sports and recreation](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10087)

[Camping](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10089)

## Product description

A small, portable butane burner appliance that can screw onto a portable butane canister.   
  
 The product is designed with a screw thread for attachment and 3 folding legs on which to place a small cooking vessel such as a pot.   
  
 The product is for use when hiking or camping in the wilderness. 

See a list of details to help identify the product

## Reason the product is recalled

The product does not meet the required gas safety standard. The threaded component may be difficult to connect to the butane canister.  
  
  

## The hazards to consumers

Gas can leak for longer than the expected short burst when screwing the product onto the canister. If this occurs near an ignition source, the released flammable gas may ignite resulting in a fire or serious illness, injury or death.  
  

## What consumers should do

Customers must stop using the product immediately and return it to their nearest Macpac retail store for a full refund. In addition to a refund, Macpac is offering customers a $20 store voucher upon returning the product.  
  
 For further information, consumers can contact Macpac Australia on 1800 325 215 or email customerservice@macpac.com.au or go to https://www.macpac.com.au/product-recall.html

# Macpac Micro-Stove

Macpac NZ Ltd

### Recall published

29 June 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Sports and recreation](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10087)

[Camping](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10089)

## Product description

A small, portable butane burner appliance that can screw onto a portable butane canister.   
  
 The product is designed with a screw thread for attachment and 3 folding legs on which to place a small cooking vessel such as a pot.   
  
 The product is for use when hiking or camping in the wilderness. 

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 7: Photograph of Underneath Macpac Micro-Stove](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Underneath%20Macpac%20Micro-Stove.jpg?itok=MtJAkfVt)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Underneath%20Macpac%20Micro-Stove.jpg?itok=9LaXIk2-)[![Image 8: Photograph of Macpac Micro-Stove Side](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20Side.jpg?itok=AKYdiBuQ)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20Side.jpg?itok=t1t4FOrK)[![Image 9: Photograph of Macpac Micro-Stove with Packaging](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20with%20Packaging.jpg?itok=HkbPaL8o)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Macpac%20Micro-Stove%20with%20Packaging.jpg?itok=ehhU_V1W)

## Reason the product is recalled

The product does not meet the required gas safety standard. The threaded component may be difficult to connect to the butane canister.  
  
  

## The hazards to consumers

Gas can leak for longer than the expected short burst when screwing the product onto the canister. If this occurs near an ignition source, the released flammable gas may ignite resulting in a fire or serious illness, injury or death.  
  

## What consumers should do

Customers must stop using the product immediately and return it to their nearest Macpac retail store for a full refund. In addition to a refund, Macpac is offering customers a $20 store voucher upon returning the product.  
  
 For further information, consumers can contact Macpac Australia on 1800 325 215 or email customerservice@macpac.com.au or go to https://www.macpac.com.au/product-recall.html

# Apache RTC1 Camper MY2019

Jaha Holdings Pty Ltd

### Recall published

16 February 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

Sports and recreation

[Camping](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10089)

[Vehicle accessories (registered)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10104)

[Caravan, motorhome and camper accessories](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10107)

## Product description

Apache RTC1 Camper  
 Model Year 2019  
  
 16 affected camper vans

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Titan Apache RTC1 Camper](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=WkId2cnp)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=kzcWNDII)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the camper.  
  
 The gas appliances have not been installed in accordance with the gas safety standard for installation in caravans and boats for non-propulsive purposes:  
  
 1. There is no gas escape hole installed for the cooker and refrigerator in accordance with the manufacturer's installation instructions.  
 2. The ventilation system for the refrigerator has not been installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s installation instructions.  

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, unburnt gas could build up in the refrigerator rear cavity that could result in a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using all gas appliances immediately and contact the manufacturer and arrange for inspection/rectification of the gas installation.   
  
 For further information, consumers can contact the manufacturer Jaha Holdings Pty Ltd on   
 07 3888 0360 or email service@caravanrsc.com.au

# Apache RTC1 Camper MY2019

Jaha Holdings Pty Ltd

### Recall published

16 February 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

Sports and recreation

[Camping](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10089)

[Vehicle accessories (registered)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10104)

[Caravan, motorhome and camper accessories](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10107)

## Product description

Apache RTC1 Camper  
 Model Year 2019  
  
 16 affected camper vans

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Titan Apache RTC1 Camper](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=WkId2cnp)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Titan%20Apache%20RTC1%20Camper.jpg?itok=kzcWNDII)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the camper.  
  
 The gas appliances have not been installed in accordance with the gas safety standard for installation in caravans and boats for non-propulsive purposes:  
  
 1. There is no gas escape hole installed for the cooker and refrigerator in accordance with the manufacturer's installation instructions.  
 2. The ventilation system for the refrigerator has not been installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s installation instructions.  

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, unburnt gas could build up in the refrigerator rear cavity that could result in a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using all gas appliances immediately and contact the manufacturer and arrange for inspection/rectification of the gas installation.   
  
 For further information, consumers can contact the manufacturer Jaha Holdings Pty Ltd on   
 07 3888 0360 or email service@caravanrsc.com.au

Queensland

# Millard Slide On Caravans

Bilsen GMW Pty Ltd

### Recall published

8 March 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Vehicle accessories (registered)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10104)

[Caravan, motorhome and camper accessories](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10107)

## Product description

Millard Slide On Caravan

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of Millard Slide On Caravan](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=xb1FsayC)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=QNpC9tzU)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the caravan as the consumer gas piping is located inside the caravan.  
  
 The consumer gas piping has not been installed in accordance with the relevant gas safety standard for installation in caravans for non-propulsive purposes.

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, gas may accumulate within the caravan and may present a risk of poisoning or a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using gas in their caravan and contact an authorised Millard Caravan Dealer to arrange for the gas piping to be rerouted, free of charge.   
  
 To locate an authorised dealer, visit http://www.millardrv.com.au/dealers.aspx  
  
 For further information, consumers can contact Millard Caravans on 02 9829 2055 or http://www.millardrv.com.au/contact.aspx

# Millard Slide On Caravans

Bilsen GMW Pty Ltd

### Recall published

8 March 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Vehicle accessories (registered)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10104)

[Caravan, motorhome and camper accessories](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10107)

## Product description

Millard Slide On Caravan

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of Millard Slide On Caravan](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=xb1FsayC)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Millard%20Slide%20On%20Caravan.png?itok=QNpC9tzU)

## Reason the product is recalled

Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is a colourless, highly flammable gas that may leak and build up inside the caravan as the consumer gas piping is located inside the caravan.  
  
 The consumer gas piping has not been installed in accordance with the relevant gas safety standard for installation in caravans for non-propulsive purposes.

## The hazards to consumers

In the event of an LPG gas leak, gas may accumulate within the caravan and may present a risk of poisoning or a fire, which could cause serious illness, injury or death.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should stop using gas in their caravan and contact an authorised Millard Caravan Dealer to arrange for the gas piping to be rerouted, free of charge.   
  
 To locate an authorised dealer, visit http://www.millardrv.com.au/dealers.aspx  
  
 For further information, consumers can contact Millard Caravans on 02 9829 2055 or http://www.millardrv.com.au/contact.aspx

## Details to help identify the product

### Who is running the recall

Bilsen GMW Pty Ltd

### Who sold the product

Millard Caravan Dealers

### Dates available for sale

15 January 2010 - 15 January 2019

### Where the product was sold

Nationally

## Responsible regulators

Regulators are established or appointed by government. They enforce regulations and rules.

**Quote PRA number 2020/18098** when contacting a regulator about this recall.

Contact the [Australian Competition and Consumer Commission](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/about-us/contact-us) if you have:

# Chant Gas Hose Assembly model A003 as attached to Jumbuck Stardom 4 Burner BBQ model HS884502

Pacific Gas & Heating Pty Ltd

### Recall published

10 March 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Home and garden](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10044)

[Outdoor furniture and barbecues](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10057)

## Product description

Chant Gas Hose Assembly model number A003  
  
 As attached to Jumbuck Stardom 4 Burner BBQ model number HS-884502  
  
 All hose assemblies attached to a Jumbuck Stardom 4B BBQ, under the coverage of AGA certificate 8169G, with a manufacture year and month of 2019/06. The month of manufacture is stated on the data label located inside the cabinet door.  
  
 Sold through Bunnings Warehouse stores between 5 August 2019 and 23 January 2020

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 6: Photograph of Chant Gas Hose Assembly](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Chant%20Gas%20Hose%20Assembly.jpg?itok=tEH_yQf2)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Chant%20Gas%20Hose%20Assembly.jpg?itok=DJJ0pqMf)

## Reason the product is recalled

The last thread of the handwheel on the hose assembly may not be completely machined. A hose assembly with this fault will not seal correctly with an LPG cylinder and gas may leak from the connection point.

## The hazards to consumers

Risk of leaking gas at the connection with an LPG cylinder could lead to burns and/or a fire and/or explosion, which may result in serious injury.

## What consumers should do

Consumers should immediately turn off the gas supply and disconnect the hose assembly from the LPG cylinder.  
 Check the date of purchase and the month and year of manufacture of their BBQ. If in is range, do not use the BBQ and contact Pacific Gas & Heating on 1300 793 978 to receive instructions on how to disconnect the hose assembly from the BBQ.  
  
 Consumers can either:  
 1. Request that Pacific Gas & Heating mail a replacement hose assembly to their home address.  
 2. Take the hose assembly to any Bunnings store to receive a replacement hose assembly.   
  
 For further information, contact Pacific Gas & Heating on 1300 793 978 or email at info@pacificgas.com.au

# Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve and Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve with Hose and Regulator

Mayo Hardware

### Recall published

18 August 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

## Product description

Grillman Gas safety shut off valve with POL fitting (sold with or without hose and regulator). Suitable for gas barbecues and outdoor gas heaters.   

### Brand

Grillman

See a list of details to help identify the product

## Reason the product is recalled

The tail pipe and main body of the valve may come apart. This may cause the seal at this point to break and allow gas to escape when the valve to the gas cylinder is open. The defect is only in the valve. The hose and regulator are not affected.  
  

## The hazards to consumers

Risk of leaking gas igniting, leading to burns and/or a fire and/or explosion, which may result in serious injury or death.  
  

## What consumers should do

Consumers should immediately stop using the products and return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.  
  
 For further information, contact Mayo Hardware on 1300 360 211 or email grillmangas@mayohardware.com.au

# Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve and Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve with Hose and Regulator

Mayo Hardware

### Recall published

18 August 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

## Product description

Grillman Gas safety shut off valve with POL fitting (sold with or without hose and regulator). Suitable for gas barbecues and outdoor gas heaters.   

### Brand

Grillman

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of GMGSG Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/GMGSG%20Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve.jpg?itok=EJEAjf0h)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/GMGSG%20Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve.jpg?itok=qisLeEQe)

[![Image 6: Photograph of Grillman Gas Safety Shut Off Valve and Regulator GMGSGREG](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve%20and%20Regulator%20GMGSGREG.jpg?itok=-FLcsIAl)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Grillman%20Gas%20Safety%20Shut%20Off%20Valve%20and%20Regulator%20GMGSGREG.jpg?itok=Z59sZrqg)[![Image 7: Photograph of identifying number 2018_01](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Identifying%20number%202018_01.jpg?itok=ye9J0SvE)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Identifying%20number%202018_01.jpg?itok=gjVYbs3u)[![Image 8: Photograph of Identifying number 2018_03](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Identifying%20number%202018_03.jpg?itok=eFSUU5xZ)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Identifying%20number%202018_03.jpg?itok=3fgiSu8E)

## Reason the product is recalled

The tail pipe and main body of the valve may come apart. This may cause the seal at this point to break and allow gas to escape when the valve to the gas cylinder is open. The defect is only in the valve. The hose and regulator are not affected.  
  

## The hazards to consumers

Risk of leaking gas igniting, leading to burns and/or a fire and/or explosion, which may result in serious injury or death.  
  

## What consumers should do

Consumers should immediately stop using the products and return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.  
  
 For further information, contact Mayo Hardware on 1300 360 211 or email grillmangas@mayohardware.com.au

# Slide Out Kitchen

Lotus Caravans

### Recall published

28 July 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Vehicle accessories (registered)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10104)

[Caravan, motorhome and camper accessories](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10107)

## Product description

An external slide out kitchen/cooking facility with a modified Weber Q 1000 barbeque and fitted as an accessory to certain caravans 

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of Slide Out Kitchen](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Slide%20Out%20Kitchen.png?itok=cBnwgT8E)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Slide%20Out%20Kitchen.png?itok=GsP--UWn)

## Reason the product is recalled

The barbeque was modified to facilitate its installation. This has resulted in the temperature of the surrounding stainless steel surfaces exceeding the relevant gas standard's requirements.   

## The hazards to consumers

If the surfaces overheat, there is an increased risk of burn injuries. 

## What consumers should do

Customers should stop using their Slide Out Kitchen and contact their closest Lotus Caravans dealership to schedule an appointment for rectification.   
  
 For more information, contact Lotus Caravans on 03 9305 3907 or via the web form at https://www.lotuscaravans.com.au/contact-us/

# Slide Out Kitchen

Lotus Caravans

### Recall published

28 July 2020

### Topics

Gas products and appliances

[Vehicle accessories (registered)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10104)

[Caravan, motorhome and camper accessories](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/recalls?f%5B0%5D=topic%3A10107)

## Product description

An external slide out kitchen/cooking facility with a modified Weber Q 1000 barbeque and fitted as an accessory to certain caravans 

See a list of details to help identify the product

[![Image 5: Photograph of Slide Out Kitchen](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/media_library/private/Slide%20Out%20Kitchen.png?itok=cBnwgT8E)](https://www.productsafety.gov.au/system/files/styles/wide/private/Slide%20Out%20Kitchen.png?itok=GsP--UWn)

## Reason the product is recalled

The barbeque was modified to facilitate its installation. This has resulted in the temperature of the surrounding stainless steel surfaces exceeding the relevant gas standard's requirements.   

## The hazards to consumers

If the surfaces overheat, there is an increased risk of burn injuries. 

## What consumers should do

Customers should stop using their Slide Out Kitchen and contact their closest Lotus Caravans dealership to schedule an appointment for rectification.   
  
 For more information, contact Lotus Caravans on 03 9305 3907 or via the web form at https://www.lotuscaravans.com.au/contact-us/
